name: io.github.library-x/tuney
title: Tuney
description: Royalty-free music fitted to your length or video: find, generate and adjust tracks, score videos.

tools.name: list_styles
tools.description:
List the genres, moods and tempos Tuney can find or generate music for.

        Call this before find_tracks or generate_track and pick the values that fit the user's brief.

tools.name: find_tracks
tools.description:
Find ready-made Tuney tracks that match a brief. Previews are free.

        Best results: pass genre, mood and tempo values from list_styles (any one is enough). A
        free-text prompt works too, but it is matched on overall feel only, not on instruments, so
        check the genre, mood and tempo of what comes back. Each result has a cue_id and a preview
        URL. limit is 1 to 5; each result takes a few seconds. Pass the returned search_id to get
        more results for the same brief. Use adjust_track to change length or key, and
        download_track for the final file.

tools.name: generate_track
tools.description:
Compose a brand-new track from Tuney's hand-made musical elements, fitted to an exact length.

        Use genre, mood and tempo values from list_styles, or leave them empty for any style.
        Generation runs in the background: this returns a task_id, so call wait_for_task next.
        Previews are free.

tools.name: get_task
tools.description:
Check a background task once: a generation, a download, or a video import, analysis, scoring or render.

        Prefer wait_for_task, which polls for you.

tools.name: wait_for_task
tools.description:
Wait for a background task to finish, reporting progress along the way.

        kind is the one the starting tool returned: generate, download, import_video, analyze_video,
        score_video or render_video. Returns the finished track (with preview_url), the download_url,
        or the video result. If it is still running when the timeout passes, the result says so:
        call wait_for_task again with the same task_id and kind.

tools.name: get_track
tools.description: Get a track by cue_id: name, preview URL, length, bpm, key, style and sections.

tools.name: adjust_track
tools.description:
Re-render a track with changes, keeping it musically coherent.

        - length_seconds: fit the track to an exact duration (the engine recomposes the arrangement).
        - turning_point_seconds: add a turning point at that second, where the music changes character
          (new arrangement after the point, an audible transition). Combine with length_seconds to
          lengthen a track and place the turning point in one go. If the track already has a turning
          point, this moves it.
        - ending: how the track ends, "fade_out" or "short" (a stab on the last beat). The track keeps
          its length (or the length_seconds you give) within a quarter of a second either way.
        - time_stretch: tempo factor, for example 0.9 slower or 1.1 faster.
        - pitch_shift: semitones, for example -2 or 3.
        - mute / unmute: stems by name: melody, chords, bass, drums.
        - regenerate: stems to re-pick musical material for (melody, chords, bass, drums); all four
          give a fresh take on the same brief.
        Runs in the background: returns a task_id for wait_for_task.

tools.name: download_track
tools.description:
Get a download link for the final file: mp3, wav, or a zip of stems.

        Signed in, this spends Tuney credits and the file is clean. Without sign-in it is free and
        the file has the pulsing tone over it (the result says listen_only).
        Returns download_url right away when the file is cached, otherwise a task_id to pass to
        wait_for_task with kind="download". Links expire, so share them promptly. download_url is on
        the Tuney API host; download_direct_url is the same file in Cloud Storage.
        For format="stems" the link is a zip with one mp3 per part; the result's `contents` map
        gives the readable name of each file (melody, chords, bass, drums, swoosh fx, impact fx).
        To show stems to the user: fetch the zip, unzip it, rename the files with that map and
        attach them. Never download the same track twice.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Show whether the user is signed in to Tuney, which account it is, and its credit balance with a link to buy more.

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description:
Start signing in to Tuney. Signed in, audio is clean (no pulsing tone) and the user has their own library and credits.

        Call it only when the user asks to sign in or wants clean files; everything works without it.
        Without a sign-in, this call makes the app show its Tuney sign-in (in Claude Code the user
        picks Authenticate for Tuney under /mcp), where an account is free to create. Tell the user
        first: some apps pause the Tuney tools until the sign-in is finished.
        When already signed in, it says so. Then call get_track with the cue_id of each track made
        before the sign-in: it comes back clean, under a new cue_id in the user's library. Render a
        video again to get clean music under it.

tools.name: get_video_upload_link
tools.description:
Create a one-time link for sending a video file (MP4, MOV or M4V) to Tuney for scoring.

        Use this when the video is a local file, for example one the user attached or one in the
        working directory. Send the file with the curl command in `example` (HTTP PUT of the raw
        file); the response contains the video_id to pass to score_video. If the video is already
        online, use import_video with its link instead.

tools.name: import_video
tools.description:
Bring a video into Tuney from a public https link that returns the file itself (not a web page).

        Returns the video_id to pass to score_video, analyze_video or render_video. Videos up to
        200 MB and 10 minutes. For a local file, use get_video_upload_link instead.

tools.name: analyze_video
tools.description:
Show what Tuney sees in a video: picture cuts with their strength, where people speak, and a sonic-logo guess.

        Optional: score_video analyses the video by itself. Use this to discuss the edit with the user
        first, for example to pick the turning point or the moment the music should end.

tools.name: score_video
tools.description:
Compose music to a video and, by default, return the video with the music under it.

        Tuney finds the picture cuts, speech and sonic logo, then arranges a track to them: the music
        ends where the logo starts (or at the end), the turning point lands on the strongest cut in
        the middle, hits land on other strong cuts outside speech, and the music is lowered while
        people speak in the rendered video.

        - prompt: describe the music ("upbeat pop for a sneaker ad"); or cue_id: one of the user's tracks.
        - ending: "fade" lands exactly on the length; "short" ends on a stab.
        - turning_point_seconds / no_turning_point: override the automatic turning point.
        - music_end_seconds / logo_start_seconds: where the music must stop (a sonic logo starts).
        - hits: sound effects on strong cuts; render: also return the scored video.

        Scoring takes about a minute; if the result says timed_out, call wait_for_task with the
        task_id and kind="score_video". The result has the track (preview_url), the plan, and the
        video link when rendered. Previews and renders are free; downloading the track costs credits.

tools.name: render_video
tools.description:
Put one of the user's tracks under a video, for example after adjust_track changed the scored track.

        duck lowers the music while people speak. music_volume and video_volume are gains from 0 to 2
        (1 leaves the level unchanged). Returns a link to the rendered MP4.
